title: CBI Brings Haryana Murder Accused Ashish Kumar Back From Kazakhstan
excerpt: An INTERPOL Red Notice issued in September led officers to Ashish Kumar at Almaty immigration; Haryana Police took him into custody on arrival in New Delhi on November 23.
body:
• Ashish Kumar, wanted in a November 2025 Haryana murder case, arrived in New Delhi on November 23 and was taken into custody by Haryana Police after being deported from Kazakhstan.
  • An INTERPOL Red Notice published in September 2026, at Haryana Police's request, led to Kumar being geo-located at immigration in Almaty, Kazakhstan, the CBI said.
  • The CBI coordinated the return with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and Haryana Police through INTERPOL channels and its BHARATPOL platform.
  • Since 2019, more than 300 wanted criminals, including 75 fugitives so far in 2026, have been brought back to India through INTERPOL channels, according to the CBI.

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) has secured the deportation of Ashish Kumar, a fugitive wanted in a Haryana murder case, from Kazakhstan to India. Kumar arrived in New Delhi on Monday, November 23, where Haryana Police took him into custody, the CBI said in a statement reported by IANS and Mirror Now.

The return was coordinated by the CBI with the Ministry of External Affairs, the Ministry of Home Affairs and Haryana Police. The CBI acts as India's National Central Bureau for INTERPOL and coordinates with law enforcement agencies across the country through BHARATPOL, its platform for international police cooperation.

The case against Kumar

Kumar was wanted in connection with a murder case registered by Haryana Police in November 2025. According to the CBI, a dispute arose between the deceased and Kumar during a marriage function. After the argument, as the deceased was returning from the venue, Kumar and his associates allegedly stopped his vehicle midway and assaulted him. The assault caused fatal injuries, and the victim died.

Kumar is an accused in the case and has not been convicted; the allegations will now be tested in court proceedings in India.

How the Red Notice found him

At the request of Haryana Police, a Red Notice was published against Kumar in September 2026 through INTERPOL channels. A Red Notice alerts police forces worldwide that a person is wanted for prosecution and asks them to locate and provisionally arrest the person pending legal proceedings.

Kumar was subsequently geo-located at Almaty immigration in Kazakhstan, the CBI said, and was deported to India. On arrival in New Delhi, Haryana Police officials took him into custody to proceed with the investigation and prosecution.

A wider run of returns

The CBI said more than 300 wanted criminals have been brought back to India through INTERPOL channels since 2019, including 75 fugitives so far during 2026. The agency said earlier this month it had also secured the deportation of a Red Notice subject from the United Arab Emirates to India on November 20, in coordination with the foreign and home ministries and Maharashtra Police.

For families of victims in cases where an accused leaves India, the Red Notice route is the formal channel: the investigating state police force requests the notice, the CBI publishes it through INTERPOL, and a locating country can then deport or extradite the person under its own law.

What happens next

Kumar is in Haryana Police custody. The next steps — production before a court, police remand proceedings and the filing of charges — rest with Haryana Police and the courts. The CBI's role in the case, as India's INTERPOL bureau, was the international coordination that brought him back.
